basis: Carcinoma occupies the adrenal medulla; the distant primary site is unspecified.
Breast carcinoma; breast has no axis, and stromal fibrosis does not establish locomotor involvement.
Autoimmune blistering skin disease. Associated celiac enteropathy is separately diagnosed; anemia and fractures do not establish direct blood or bone injury.
Radiation directly injures pulmonary tissue. Inflammation from radiation alone does not establish an immune-mediated disease.
Disordered glucose metabolism; future diabetes and vascular complications are risks rather than defining organ damage.
Developmental disability and skeletal malformations define the syndrome. Cardiac defects and myeloproliferation occur in 5-29%; facial and skin-fold variants do not imply damage.
SCALP denotes sebaceous nevus, CNS malformations, aplasia cutis, limbal dermoid and pigmented nevus; skin, brain and ocular lesions define the syndrome.
Defined by developmental delay and epileptiform brain dysfunction; no other organ damage is established.
Impaired cortical recognition of visually perceived objects; this is neurologic dysfunction rather than damage to the eye.
Peroxisomal disease with cortical malformations and hepatopathy; tricuspid regurgitation in 2/4 supports cardiac involvement. Individual ocular and renal findings occur in 1/4.
Loss of dim-light vision is a retinal visual-function disorder.
Ichthyosis defines the disease; developmental disability occurs in 30-79%. Typical corneal deposits usually spare vision; renal and endocrine abnormalities occur in 5-29%.
Gonadal sex cord-stromal tumor arising from Sertoli endocrine/supporting cells; estrogenic or androgenic secretion may occur.
Lung, brain and liver disease define the syndrome; thin bone cortices and delayed skeletal maturation in 7/7 support skeletal involvement. Anemia in 7/7 omitted under the four-axis cap.
Malignant neuroendocrine tumor of the carotid-body paraganglion. The adjacent carotid artery is not its tissue of origin; metastatic sites are unspecified.
Arterial aneurysms and skeletal/connective-tissue abnormalities define LDS1. Soft skin, blue sclerae and facial variants alone do not establish additional organ damage.
Inherited Alzheimer neurodegeneration causing progressive cognitive loss.
Genetic podocyte disease causing proteinuria and nephrotic syndrome; edema and hypoalbuminemia do not establish other organ damage.
Chronic lymphatic vascular obstruction causes marked dermal and subcutaneous enlargement and fibrosis. Infection is only one cause across this umbrella.
Mitochondrial metabolic myopathy directly affects extraocular and eyelid muscles, producing progressive loss of ocular movement.
Muscle hypoplasia, weakness, contractures and skeletal anomalies define the syndrome. Abnormal dermatoglyphics do not imply skin damage; valve involvement has unspecified frequency.
Inherited aldosterone excess with defining hypertension in 80-99%. Stroke, retinopathy and ventricular hypertrophy are occasional, separately recognized complications.
Malignant neoplasm affecting short bones of the lower limb.
Lysosomal lipid storage with late-infantile neurodegeneration; hepatic disease, including earlier cholestasis, affects roughly 30-50%. Splenic enlargement alone is not blood dysfunction.
Fibroblastic sarcoma arising in deep soft connective tissues; no additional organ involvement is specified.
